report.tagline: A paid app for sleep, meditation and relaxation, best known for Sleep Stories read by famous voices, now also sold to employers and health plans as Calm Health.
report.simpleSummary: Calm is an app you open when you want to fall asleep, calm down or meditate. It has guided meditations, music, nature sounds and Sleep Stories, which are bedtime stories for adults read by actors and celebrities. A few things are free, but most content needs a subscription of about $70 a year. Calm also sells a version called Calm Health to employers and health insurers, who give it to their staff or members for free.

overview.whatItDoes: Calm offers audio and video content to help people sleep better, feel less anxious and build a meditation habit. Users get a daily guided session (Daily Calm), Sleep Stories, music, breathing exercises and courses. It earns mostly from consumer subscriptions, and increasingly from Calm Health, a version sold to employers and health plans that adds mental health screening and care programmes.
howItWorks: A new user downloads the app, answers a short question about their goal (sleep, stress, focus) and starts a free trial.
After the trial, the app charges an annual or monthly subscription through the App Store, Google Play or the website.
Users play a Daily Calm meditation in the morning or a Sleep Story at night; streaks and reminders encourage daily use.
New content is added every week, including celebrity Sleep Stories and music.
Employers and health plans pay Calm to offer Calm Health to their members free of charge.
Calm also earns from partnerships and products, such as bedding sold at Target.
overview.valueProposition: A calm, beautiful app that helps you fall asleep and feel less stressed in a few minutes a day, without therapy or medicine.

businessModel.summary: Calm makes most of its money from annual consumer subscriptions, paid after a free trial. Its second engine is Calm Health, sold to employers and health plans per member. Content is made once and listened to millions of times, so the cost of serving each extra user is low.

revenueStreams.detail: Mostly annual plans around $70 in the US, plus monthly and lifetime options.
Fees from employers, health plans and providers per covered member.
Bedding at Target, hotel partnerships and branded content deals.

businessModel.pricing: Free trial, then about $70 a year or about $15 a month in the US (before the February 2026 increase); a lifetime plan is also offered. Calm Health pricing is not public.
costDrivers: Performance marketing on social media and app stores
App store fees of up to 30% on in-app payments
Enterprise sales and clinical staff for Calm Health
businessModel.unitEconomics: A US subscriber paying $70 a year through the App Store leaves Calm with about $49 to $59 after Apple's 15% to 30% cut. Streaming audio costs very little. The big cost is CAC, the money spent on ads to win that subscriber, which can be tens of dollars. If the user renews for a second year, Calm earns that $50 or so again with almost no marketing cost, so renewal is where profit comes from. Many users stop after year one, which is why Calm pushes habits and B2B deals.

howTheyGetUsers: Paid social and app store ads
Brand moments, like Sleep Stories read by celebrities
Partnerships, such as free trials with bedding or hotels
Employers and health plans giving Calm to millions of members
growth.moat: Calm's moat is its brand and a large library of high-quality, original content, especially Sleep Stories. That is hard but not impossible to copy; free apps like Insight Timer and big players like Spotify and Amazon also offer sleep audio. Calm Health contracts with health plans add some stickiness.

competitors.name: Headspace
competitors.positioning: Meditation app with a strong focus on mental health care and therapy.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Calm leads on sleep content; Headspace leans more into clinical care and coaching.

competitors.name: Insight Timer
competitors.positioning: Large free meditation library with optional paid features.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Insight Timer is mostly free; Calm is polished and paid.

competitors.name: Spotify and YouTube
competitors.positioning: Free or bundled sleep sounds and meditation audio.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Calm offers structured programmes and original content, but must justify a separate fee.

competitors.name: Amazon Sleep Studio
competitors.positioning: Sleep content at about $5.99 a month.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Cheaper and bundled with Amazon devices; Calm has a bigger library and brand.

strengths: Leading brand in sleep and meditation
Large original content library, including Sleep Stories
Low cost to serve each extra user
Calm Health reaches about 39 million covered lives
weaknesses: Most consumer users churn after the first year
Very little free content, which can feel like a hard paywall
Depends on paid ads and app stores

Fewer downloads of mental health apps since 2022
AI tools that can make custom meditations for free
US rules on auto-renewal and easy cancellation
userComplaints: Charged for an annual renewal they did not expect
Too much locked behind the paywall

improvementIdeas.idea: Renewal reminder 7 days before charge with a summary of the user's year (minutes, sleep stories, streaks)
improvementIdeas.problem: Surprise renewal charges cause refunds and angry reviews.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer refunds and better trust; some users re-commit after seeing their progress.

improvementIdeas.idea: Personalised weekly plan that mixes new and favourite content
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More sessions per week and higher renewal.

improvementIdeas.idea: Sleep tracking link with Apple Health and wearables, showing whether Calm helped sleep
improvementIdeas.problem: Users cannot see if the app works.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Proof of value that drives renewals and B2B sales.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of subscribers with linked sleep data

improvementIdeas.problem: Many users only want sleep content and leave at the $70 price.

pmLessons: Own one clear use case. Calm grew by becoming the bedtime app, not just another meditation app.
In subscriptions, the second year is where profit is. Design for renewal, not only for trial conversion.
A pandemic boom can fade. Plan for normal demand.
Selling through employers and health plans can reach millions at once, but only pays off if people activate.

interviewQuestions.question: Calm's renewal rate is falling. How would you investigate?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment by cohort, channel, platform and usage; look at engagement before renewal; check price changes and competitors.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Calm offer more free content?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh trial conversion and CAC against brand reach and SEO; propose a test with clear success metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to help Calm users sleep better.
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a persona, define the problem (falling asleep, waking up), propose a feature, metric and guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase Calm Health activation at a new employer?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map the funnel from eligible to active, find drop-offs, use campaigns, single sign-on and manager nudges.

interviewQuestions.question: What north star would you pick for Calm?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weekly engaged subscribers over downloads or revenue; break down into acquisition, engagement, renewal and B2B.

glossary.meaning: Customer acquisition cost: how much it costs to win one paying customer.
The share of customers who stop paying in a period.
A short period of free use before a paid subscription starts.
Business to business: selling to companies instead of individual consumers.
The number of people who have access to a service through an employer or health plan.
The point where users must pay to access more content.
The one metric a company uses to track whether users are getting real value.
Something that makes it hard for competitors to copy or beat a business.

assumptions: Revenue is a rough estimate from Sacra; Calm is private and does not publish results.
The CAC example of tens of dollars is an inference from typical subscription app costs.
Monthly price of about $15 is from typical US App Store listings, not confirmed in our sources.
The claim that most consumer users churn after year one is an inference from industry patterns.
